cards.title: A blurry photo is a useless prescription
cards.body: If the chemist, the doctor or an app can't read it, the photo might as well not exist. Getting it right takes about ten seconds.

cards.title: Flat on a table, not in your hand
cards.body: Smooth out the folds and lay the paper on a plain, dark surface. Hands shake, and curled paper hides words at the edges.

cards.title: Daylight beats flash
cards.body: Stand near a window. Flash bounces off glossy paper and washes out the ink. Make sure your own shadow isn't falling across it.

cards.title: Shoot straight from above
cards.body: Hold the phone parallel to the paper so the text doesn't slant. Fit all four corners in, including the doctor's name and the date.

cards.title: Tap to focus, then check
cards.body: Tap on the handwriting before you shoot. Zoom into the photo afterwards. If you can't read the doses, take another.

cards.title: Both sides, if there's writing
cards.body: Notes often continue on the back. Photograph every page and keep them together with a caption like 'Papa, 2 pages'.

cards.title: Keep the original paper anyway
cards.body: The photo is a backup, not a replacement. In AICA, you confirm what AI reads against the photo before saving, so clear photos really help.

takeaway: Flat paper, daylight, straight from above, focus on the writing, every page, and keep the original.
share: Photographing a prescription? Flat on a table, daylight, straight from above, all four corners.
